name: Oil (Brent)
summary: Brent near $105 after a near-4% fall on 2 Nov on Doha talks; Hormuz still largely shut
state: Brent fell nearly 4% on 2 Nov to about $104.8 as Iran said a condensed plan to reopen Hormuz in exchange for ending the US blockade could be implemented within two days (Reuters); it is still 4% up on the month. Iranian sources said a new US attack looked more likely than a deal. The status stays at Alert under the board's hysteresis rule while Hormuz remains largely shut.
for_you: Expect continued high petrol, diesel and heating-oil prices, with knock-on effects on transport costs and inflation.
rubric_hit: Brent $104.8 below $110 Alert line, held by hysteresis; Hormuz largely shut

sources.title: Reuters via Investing.com — Iranians have left Doha talks, draft proposal for US deal being circulated

why: Oil feeds inflation, transport and household budgets; price spikes have preceded most post-war recessions.
drivers: OPEC+ output, Middle East supply risk, sanctions, demand, inventories, shipping disruption.

rubric.alert: Brent > $110, or 1-month change > +30%, or a major physical supply outage (> 2 mb/d).
